register.description: Which Hebrew is this. 'trade' is what a supplier or tradesperson says across a counter; 'formal' is spec-sheet / Academy Hebrew, which is often NOT what you should say out loud; 'colloquial' is street register; 'borrowed' is an English word used as-is.

id.description: Stable kebab-case key. Never reused, never renamed.

en.description: English term as Daniel would say it.

he.description: The single form to actually use. Where the useful word and the correct word differ, this is the useful one.

domain.description: Top-level area: electrical, plumbing, hardware, construction, it, telecoms, hvac, tools, commerce.

type.description: Is the Hebrew a genuine coinage, an English word in Hebrew letters, or a mix (e.g. כבל USB).

alternatives.description: Other forms you will hear or read. The Academy term usually lives here, not in `he`.

note.description: When this form is used instead, and by whom.

gloss.description: What the thing actually is, in English, for when the translation alone does not settle it.

example_he.description: A sentence you would really say in a shop.

notes.description: Usage traps: false friends, terms falling out of favour, what the counter staff will assume you mean.

seen_at.description: Provenance. Repo-relative paths to source screenshots, and/or URLs.

confidence.description: How sure the machine pass is. Low-confidence entries are the queue for human review.

human_notes.description: What a native speaker said when they reviewed it.
